title: ufws-world-heavyweight
label: Sargent “Sledge” Hammer
how: Won the vacant title in the final of the opening night's twelve-man tournament, pinning Death with a shoulder throw. Lost it seven weeks later to Ford Firepower, in 9:19 — the federation's own results desk: “Sledge Hammer lost the World title after seven weeks on the top of the world.”

title: ufws-world-heavyweight
label: Ford Firepower
how: Captured the title at 9:19 in his second match in the federation; lost it nine days later when Billy Thunder pinned him at 4:29.

title: ufws-world-heavyweight
label: Billy Thunder
how: Pinned Ford Firepower at 4:29 in his third match. Lost the belt to Running Eagle Feather inside the unheld Report #11: Report #12 of 29 July 1991 says outright that “Billy Thunder will have a chance to regain the World belt that he dropped to Running Eagle Fetaher last week.” Report #11 does not survive. Report #10 of 18 July 1991 and Report #12 of 29 July 1991 bracket the change between them and Report #12 names its outcome outright, so the reign is chained across the gap at month precision rather than left broken.

title: ufws-world-heavyweight
label: Running Eagle Feather
how: Won the title inside the unheld Report #11, a fortnight after debuting; the change is named in Report #12's own recap. Lost it in Report #12 when the Four Corners chased his manager round the ring, the SandMan hit him with a roll of quarters behind the referee's back, and Billy Thunder hit the Thunderstorm. Report #11 does not survive. Report #10 of 18 July 1991 and Report #12 of 29 July 1991 bracket the change between them and Report #12 names its outcome outright, so the reign is chained across the gap at month precision rather than left broken.

title: ufws-world-heavyweight
label: Billy Thunder
how: A second reign, won on the Four Corners' interference and lost eight days later to Sargent Sledge Hammer in 6:30.

title: ufws-world-heavyweight
label: Sargent “Sledge” Hammer
how: A second reign for the federation's first champion, won at 6:30. He defended it against Billy Thunder again on 18 August, against the battle-royal winner John Girder at the second SuperCard, and against DiMadMan in the last issue that survives, and holds the belt where the record ends.

title: ufws-north-american-heavyweight
label: Death
how: Awarded the title as the losing finalist of the opening night's World title tournament, by that tournament's own announced rule. Lost it to Ricky Dangerous at 7:56.

title: ufws-north-american-heavyweight
label: Ricky Dangerous
how: Pinned Death at 7:56. Lost the belt in a steel cage when Mr. Mercury dived off the top of it onto him at 9:22.

title: ufws-north-american-heavyweight
label: Mr. Mercury
how: Won it in the cage rematch the federation's own president had ordered after a disqualification finish. Lost it to Cowboy Kevin Puckett's spinning toehold at 16:41.

title: ufws-north-american-heavyweight
label: “Cowboy” Kevin Puckett
how: Made Mr. Mercury submit at 16:41; lost it back to him nine days later in 2:58.

title: ufws-north-american-heavyweight
label: Mr. Mercury
how: A second reign, won in 2:58. It ended at the Summit of E-Wrestling of 10-12 July 1991 (its own wing, id `summit-of-e-wrestling`): Report #10 of 18 July opens on “last week's Summit, where we crowned a new North American champion,” and the Aztec Mummy is champion from that issue on. The match itself belongs to the Summit's own scripts, not to this wing, and is not structured here.

title: ufws-north-american-heavyweight
label: The Aztec Mummy
how: Won the belt at the Summit of E-Wrestling (its own wing, id `summit-of-e-wrestling`) and defended it in Report #10 against Johnny Vicious; for one week in July he held this title and the All-Jobber belt at the same time, the only wrestler in the federation's record to hold two. Lost it inside the unheld Report #11 to Brewster Cogburn, whom Report #12 introduces with his “brand new North American title.” Report #11 does not survive. Report #10 of 18 July 1991 and Report #12 of 29 July 1991 bracket the change between them and Report #12 names its outcome outright, so the reign is chained across the gap at month precision rather than left broken.

title: ufws-north-american-heavyweight
label: Brewster Cogburn
how: Won inside the unheld Report #11; the change is named in Report #12's own preview. Defended it against the Unknown Masked Wrestler, Jimmy Vendetta and Lightning Bolt, and lost it to Billy Thunder in the last issue that survives. Report #11 does not survive. Report #10 of 18 July 1991 and Report #12 of 29 July 1991 bracket the change between them and Report #12 names its outcome outright, so the reign is chained across the gap at month precision rather than left broken.

title: ufws-north-american-heavyweight
label: Billy Thunder
how: Took the belt in the Portland card reported in the last surviving issue, and holds it where the record ends.

title: ufws-world-tag-team
label: Crime and Punishment
how: Won the vacant belts in the opening night's tournament final, Craig Sommers rolling Ricky Dangerous up out of an abdominal stretch at 9:45. Lost them to the Masked Missiles at 8:18.

title: ufws-world-tag-team
label: The Masked Missiles
how: Chief Tomahawk pinned Grant Meadows at 8:18 after a Tomahawk Drop; nine days later Meadows superslammed him for the belts back.

title: ufws-world-tag-team
label: Crime and Punishment
how: A second reign, won at 8:18 and held for three and a half weeks before Club Anarchy took the belts in 12:50.

title: ufws-world-tag-team
label: Club Anarchy
how: Won at 12:50 on the back of three straight wins, after losing their first five matches in the federation. Held the belts through four defences, including one against the Summit's Road Warrior Cup winners, and lost them inside the unheld Report #11: Report #12 opens by calling the Shadow Assassins “the new UFWS Tag-team champions.” Report #11 does not survive. Report #10 of 18 July 1991 and Report #12 of 29 July 1991 bracket the change between them and Report #12 names its outcome outright, so the reign is chained across the gap at month precision rather than left broken.

title: ufws-world-tag-team
label: The Shadow Assassins
how: Won inside the unheld Report #11. Their only recorded defence was the one the All-Jobber Confederation broke up in a twenty-five-minute brawl, won by disqualification; they lost the belts the same night to the Ultimate Trekkies at 13:56. Report #11 does not survive. Report #10 of 18 July 1991 and Report #12 of 29 July 1991 bracket the change between them and Report #12 names its outcome outright, so the reign is chained across the gap at month precision rather than left broken.

title: ufws-world-tag-team
label: The Ultimate Trekkies
how: The Tholian Black Widow pinned Ricky Dangerous at 13:56. Four defences followed — the New Mystics, the American Guerilla, and the Long Necks twice — before Ricky Dangerous pinned the Black Widow after two DDTs on the concrete floor to take the belts back.

title: ufws-world-tag-team
label: The Shadow Assassins
how: A second reign, won in the Portland card reported in the last surviving issue, and standing where the record ends.

title: ufws-all-jobber
label: Baron Von Klaw
how: The first championship the federation ever awarded: Von Klaw took the Klaw hold on Sargent Glasnost and covered him at 4:44 in the All-Jobber tournament final, which was called before either other final. Lost it five weeks later when the Wolfman ducked his international object, took it and knocked him out with it.

title: ufws-all-jobber
label: The Wolfman
how: Won it with Von Klaw's own weapon, in the match the results desk says turned him into a fan favourite. Defended it three times in a fortnight and lost it to Bobby Windsor in 58 seconds.

title: ufws-all-jobber
label: Bobby “The Cavalier” Windsor
how: Won it in 58 seconds and defended it four times, twice against Baron Von Klaw's stablemates, before the Aztec Mummy took it with the Mummy's Claw at 1:18.

title: ufws-all-jobber
label: Bobby “The Cavalier” Windsor
how: A second reign, won inside the unheld Report #11 and defended against the Aztec Mummy in three consecutive issues — four weeks running against the same challenger, an oddity the broadcast itself complained about. Lost it to Baron Von Klaw, who kept the Klaw hold on until Windsor bled and had to be carried out. Report #11 does not survive. Report #10 of 18 July 1991 and Report #12 of 29 July 1991 bracket the change between them and Report #12 names its outcome outright, so the reign is chained across the gap at month precision rather than left broken.

title: ufws-all-jobber
label: The Aztec Mummy
how: A one-week reign held alongside the North American title — the only double championship in the federation's record. Lost the belt back to Bobby Windsor inside the unheld Report #11: Report #12's own results desk has Windsor “defending the All-Jobber title with success against the former champion, The Aztec Mummy.” Report #11 does not survive. Report #10 of 18 July 1991 and Report #12 of 29 July 1991 bracket the change between them and Report #12 names its outcome outright, so the reign is chained across the gap at month precision rather than left broken.

title: ufws-all-jobber
label: Baron Von Klaw
how: A second reign, eleven days long, ended by Sargent Glasnost's Japanese armlock in the Seattle card reported in the last surviving issue.

title: ufws-all-jobber
label: Sargent Glasnost
how: Won with the Japanese armlock over Baron Von Klaw, and holds the belt where the record ends.

title: ufws-north-american-tag-team
label: The New Mystics
how: Won the vacant title in the final of the federation's nine-team tournament, the Hunter falling on Chief Tomahawk off a Wizard dropkick. They defended it against the Long Necks three days later and hold it where the record ends.
